data.answer: This query recursively walks backward through resolved call edges from any symbol named `resolve_semantic_fks` to find every caller, including standalone functions, methods, and class-scope callers, while excluding callers located in test files. It returns each caller's fully qualified symbol ID and the shortest call depth (direct callers have depth 1). The traversal includes callback references and avoids infinite loops through cyclic calls.

data.question: What would be affected if resolve_semantic_fks changed? List every resolved caller symbol, including standalone functions, methods and class-scope callers, reached directly or indirectly, with the shortest call depth, outside the tests.
data.reference_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE impact(symbol_id, depth, path) AS (
  SELECT c.caller_symbol_id, 1, '|' || t.symbol_id || '|' || c.caller_symbol_id || '|'
  FROM code.calls c
  JOIN code.symbols t ON t.symbol_id = c.callee_symbol_id
  WHERE t.name = 'resolve_semantic_fks'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.caller_symbol_id, i.depth + 1, i.path || c.caller_symbol_id || '|'
  FROM code.calls c
  JOIN impact i ON c.callee_symbol_id = i.symbol_id
  WHERE strpos(i.path, '|' || c.caller_symbol_id || '|') = 0
)
SELECT i.symbol_id, MIN(i.depth) AS depth
FROM impact i
JOIN code.symbols s ON s.symbol_id = i.symbol_id
JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id
WHERE NOT f.is_test
GROUP BY i.symbol_id
ORDER BY depth, i.symbol_id;

request.evidence: Follow resolved calls backwards from the callee to its callers, recursively. Calls include callback references (call_kind 'callback'), where a function is passed to another call such as asyncio.to_thread(f, x). Overridden methods called through a base class (self._run_once() in a base class) are not followed to the subclass.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. Describe what the query computes and the assumptions it makes; the returned rows are reported separately. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. data.sql: WITH RECURSIVE target AS (SELECT s.symbol_id FROM code.symbols AS s WHERE s.name = 'resolve_semantic_fks'), caller_paths AS (SELECT c.caller_symbol_id AS symbol_id, 1 AS depth, list_value(c.callee_symbol_id, c.caller_symbol_id) AS path FROM code.calls AS c INNER JOIN target AS t ON c.callee_symbol_id = t.symbol_id INNER JOIN code.symbols AS s ON s.symbol_id = c.caller_symbol_id INNER JOIN code.files AS f ON f.file_id = s.file_id WHERE c.callee_symbol_id IS NOT NULL AND c.resolution IN ('same_file', 'imported', 'method_on_self') AND f.is_test = FALSE UNION SELECT c.caller_symbol_id AS symbol_id, cp.depth + 1 AS depth, list_append(cp.path, c.caller_symbol_id) AS path FROM caller_paths AS cp INNER JOIN code.calls AS c ON c.callee_symbol_id = cp.symbol_id INNER JOIN code.symbols AS s ON s.symbol_id = c.caller_symbol_id INNER JOIN code.files AS f ON f.file_id = s.file_id WHERE c.callee_symbol_id IS NOT NULL AND c.resolution IN ('same_file', 'imported', 'method_on_self') AND f.is_test = FALSE AND NOT list_contains(cp.path, c.caller_symbol_id)) SELECT symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth FROM caller_paths GROUP BY symbol_id ORDER BY depth, symbol_id
